title: Senior Rides to the Doctors: How to Catch a Ride
summary: Need a ride to the doctor? GoGoGrandparent offers safe, affordable transportation for seniors and people with disabilities—no app required. Call or schedule online today.
body_markdown:
If you're a senior who no longer drives, catching a ride to the doctor shouldn't be the hardest part of staying healthy. And if it worries you, you're far from alone. Among adults who don't have a car or public transit nearby,[more than 1 in 5 went without medical care they needed](https://www.rwjf.org/en/insights/our-research/2023/04/more-than-one-in-five-adults-with-limited-public-transit-access-forgo-healthcare-because-of-transportation-barriers.html) , according to the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. If you no longer drive and there isn't a bus route or a family car close by, that's the situation those numbers describe. The good news is you've got more options than you might think, and setting one up is easier than it sounds.


Fall is a busy season for appointments, too. Annual checkups, follow-ups, and end-of-year visits all seem to land in the same few months, so that's a lot of trips to arrange. Here's how to make every one of them simple.


## **What are your options for getting to a doctor's appointment?**


You've got several ways to get where you need to go, and each has trade-offs, so it helps to see them side by side.


- **A family member or friend.** It's free and familiar, but it means leaning on someone else's schedule, and not everyone has family nearby.
- **Public transit or a senior shuttle.** The cost is low, but routes and times are limited, and getting to the stop can be tough in bad weather.
- **Non-emergency medical transport.** It's built for medical trips and sometimes covered for certain needs, but it usually has to be booked well in advance.
- **A senior ride service like GoGoGrandparent.** You call, text, or book online, and a driver comes to your door. There's no app, no smartphone, and no waiting on anyone else's calendar.


If you don't need medical help during the trip itself, and you'd rather arrange rides on your own schedule than work around someone else's, that last option is usually the simplest to set up and the easiest to repeat. If you want to compare the bigger picture, our guide to[transportation options for seniors](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/what-are-the-transportation-options-for-senior-citizens) breaks down every choice.


## **Which kind of ride do you actually need?**


Not every trip to the doctor is the same kind of trip, and this is worth sorting out before you book anything. A regular ride and medical transport are two different services, and working out which one you need ahead of time saves a scramble on the day.


**A regular ride is usually fine when:**


- It's a routine visit. A checkup, a follow-up, lab work, a dental cleaning, an eye exam.
- Getting in and out of a car is manageable, alone or with a cane or folding walker that comes along.
- There is no sedation involved, and nobody has asked for someone to come along.


**Non-emergency medical transport is the better call when:**


- A wheelchair has to travel too, or the vehicle needs to be one that rolls straight in.
- Someone has to physically help out of the car and into the office.
- The appointment involves anesthesia or sedation. A colonoscopy, cataract surgery, an outpatient procedure of almost any kind.


That last one catches people out. The American Society of Anesthesiologists is direct about it: after sedation[you will need to arrange for someone to take you home](https://madeforthismoment.asahq.org/preparing-for-surgery/procedures/colonoscopy/) , and it is not considered safe to drive or travel on your own that day. Many clinics won't do the procedure at all unless a responsible adult is there with you, and a driver who has never met you does not count. If there's any chance the appointment falls into this category, call the office and ask what they require before booking a ride. That two-minute phone call saves a wasted trip.


And if there isn't a family member or friend who can be there, that's worth a conversation with us. Our home services team may be able to help you arrange someone to be with you. Give us a call and ask what's possible for your appointment.


## **What makes a ride service a good fit for seniors?**


The barrier for a lot of older adults isn't the ride itself. It's the technology. Standard rideshare apps assume you've got a smartphone, a credit card already loaded in, and the patience to tap through a screen while a driver waits at the curb.


A senior ride service removes that barrier. With GoGoGrandparent, you can request a ride the way you're comfortable, by phone, by text, or through a simple web chat. There's no app to download and nothing to figure out on a small screen. Your saved addresses are already there, so you're not reading out your doctor's address from an appointment card every single time.


A few practical things people ask before their first medical ride:


- **Can rides be booked ahead?** Yes. There is no sitting by the phone hoping a driver turns up free on the morning of the appointment.
- **What about the trip home?** Appointments run late, so there is no need to lock in a return time nobody can control. Many people book the trip there in advance, then call for the ride home once they're actually finished and back at the front desk.
- **What about a walker or cane?** A cane or many folding walkers will usually fit in a standard car. Mention yours when booking so there's room for it. A wheelchair that does not fold is the case for medical transport instead.


## **How does GoGoGrandparent get you to the doctor?**


GoGoGrandparent works with Uber and Lyft and matches you with highly-rated drivers, with a small concierge fee on top of the ride cost. Here's what that looks like on the day of your appointment.


- **You request the ride your way.** Call, text, or use the web chat, and tell us where you're going and when.
- **A vetted driver comes to you.** We select for drivers with high ratings, so you're not rolling the dice on who shows up.
- **Our team is there if you need it.** Our GoGo Guardians team is able to monitor your ride and step in if plans change or a driver is running late, which is real peace of mind when you're heading somewhere that matters.
- **Your family can follow along.** Family features let a loved one see when you're picked up and dropped off, and that helps a lot if your kids live in another city.


The goal is simple. You get to your appointment on time, and nobody has to rearrange their whole day to make it happen.


## **What should you plan before your medical ride?**


Five minutes of planning is the difference between an easy appointment and a stressful one. Here's what's worth sorting out the day before.


1. **Check the exact address, not just the practice name.** Big medical groups run several buildings, and the suite number on an appointment card may not match the address on the website. Large hospital campuses are the worst for this. Ask which entrance is the right one.
2. **Allow more time than seems necessary.** Traffic, the drop-off, finding the right floor, and checking in all take longer than the drive does. Leaving thirty minutes early costs a magazine in a waiting room. Leaving ten minutes early can cost the appointment.
3. **Decide the return trip in advance.** Not the time, the plan. Know whether it's a phone call once the appointment ends or a family member collecting. The worst moment to work this out is standing at the front desk feeling tired.
4. **Say what's coming along.** A walker, a cane, a portable oxygen tank, a folded wheelchair. Mention it at booking so the right vehicle turns up.
5. **Ask the office about an escort.** Where sedation is involved, most clinics require a responsible adult, and some will cancel on the day if a patient arrives alone. Ask when making the appointment, not the night before.


Write the answers on the appointment card itself. It's the one piece of paper that will definitely be in a pocket on the day.


## **What if you need more than a ride to the doctor?**


Getting to the doctor is often just one piece of staying healthy at home. The prescription still needs picking up, the fridge still needs filling, and when the weather turns cold, those errands only get harder.


GoGoGrandparent is more than rides. The same service can help with[grocery delivery](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/best-ways-for-seniors-to-get-groceries) ,[meal delivery](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/best-meal-delivery-services-for-seniors-with-diabetes-special-diets) , and[pharmacy delivery](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/how-to-get-prescriptions-delivered) , so the things you need can come to you instead. That matters more once the weather turns. Wherever you live, the months when it gets dark at five, or rains for a week, or turns bitterly cold are the months when a quick errand stops being quick. You can keep the appointment in person and let the rest come to the door.


## **How do you set up your first ride?**


Getting started takes only a few minutes.


1. **Sign up by phone or online.** You can register over the phone with a real person, or on the website if you'd rather do it yourself.
2. **Save your common places.** Add your doctor's office, pharmacy, and home so future rides are quick to book.
3. **Request your ride.** Call, text, or use the web chat whenever you need to go. That's it.


Once you're set up, every future appointment is one quick call away.


## **Stay independent, stay moving**


Giving up driving doesn't mean giving up your freedom. It means finding a dependable way to keep doing what matters, and that starts with taking care of your health. With the right ride in place, you can keep every appointment, stay on top of your care, and do it all on your own terms.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How do seniors get to doctor appointments if they don't drive?**


Seniors have several options, including family and friends, public transit or senior shuttles, non-emergency medical transport, and senior ride services like GoGoGrandparent. A ride service is often the easiest to set up, since you can book by phone, text, or web chat and a driver comes to your door.


### **Can you book a ride to a doctor's appointment in advance?**


Yes. You can arrange the ride ahead of time rather than waiting until the morning of your appointment. Many people book the trip there in advance and then call for the ride home once the appointment actually finishes, since appointments often run late.


### **Can you take a regular ride home after a procedure with anesthesia?**


Usually not. If you're having a procedure with sedation or anesthesia, most clinics require a responsible adult to accompany you home, and a driver doesn't meet that requirement. Ask the office what they require when you book the appointment, because some will cancel on the day if you arrive without an escort. If you don't have someone who can be there, ask us about home services. Our home services team may be able to help you arrange support.


### **Do you need a smartphone to use GoGoGrandparent?**


No. You can request a ride by phone, by text, or through a simple web chat. There's no app to download and nothing to tap through on a small screen, which is why it works well for seniors who don't use a smartphone.


### **Can a family member arrange the ride for me?**


Yes. A family member can help set up your account and arrange rides, and family features let them see when you're picked up and dropped off. That's especially helpful when your loved ones live far away.


### **Is someone keeping an eye on the ride?**


Our GoGo Guardians team is able to monitor your ride and step in if plans change or a driver is delayed, so you're not on your own once the trip starts.


### **Can GoGoGrandparent help with more than rides to the doctor?**


Yes. Along with rides, GoGoGrandparent can help with grocery, meal, and pharmacy delivery, so the essentials can come to you. That's especially useful in the colder months, when getting out for errands is harder.
